Baldur's Gate 3 · Script Extender mod · Patch 8

Loot Advisor Handbook

The right gear for your build, and where to find it: rainbow frames, rainbow map markers, an item list and a live Sets page in your browser.

Loot Advisor

Hotkey
F6 item list
For
the 7 origin characters
Needs
Script Extender v33 or newer for frames and map painting

New here? Read Before you start to install Script Extender and the mod, then Loot Advisor for what you see in the game. The mod is free; source and updates: https://github.com/md12ol/LootAdvisor.

Before you start

Loot Advisor is a Script Extender mod. Install Script Extender once, then the mod, and it works from the next game start.

Script Extender and a mod manager

  1. Get BG3 Mod Manager (free). In it, choose Tools > Download and Extract the Script Extender. That installs BG3 Script Extender in one click. Loot Advisor's marks inside the game's own interface need version 33 or newer; until v33 is a normal release, get it from the Devel channel: create a file ScriptExtenderUpdaterConfig.json in the game's bin folder containing {"UpdateChannel": "Devel"}, then start the game once. Delete that file to go back to normal releases. Script Extender is a separate community project and is not included with this mod.
  2. Drag LootAdvisor.pak into BG3 Mod Manager (or File > Import Mod), move Loot Advisor to the active mods list, then Save Load Order and Export Load Order to Game.
  3. Start the game. If a Mod Verification dialog lists Loot Advisor, tick it and choose Start Game.

Installing by hand works too: copy the pak to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Larian Studios\Baldur's Gate 3\Mods\ and enable it in the load order (a mod manager is the safe way to edit modsettings.lsx). The chapter below has the details for Loot Advisor.

What is in this folder

FileWhat it is
LootAdvisor.pakThe mod. This is the only file the game needs.
INSTALL.mdThe install steps in short.
Handbook.htmlThis handbook. It works offline.
Page/Sets.htmlA copy of the Sets page. Opened from this folder it tells you to load a save once and gives the path of the live page that the mod writes (see The Sets page).
Media/The banner, thumbnail, logo marks and screenshots, for sharing or a mod page. The game does not need them.

Viewing the Sets page next to the game

  • From the game: press F6, then Open Sets page in the item list: click the path it shows, press Ctrl+C and paste it into your browser's address bar. Or open your bookmark of the page (load a save once first; the mod writes the page then).
  • Two monitors: play in Borderless Window (the game's Video settings) and keep the browser on the second monitor. The page follows the game by itself.
  • One monitor: open the Steam overlay browser (Shift+Tab, then the web browser) and open the page there, or switch to your browser with Alt+Tab (smoothest in Borderless Window).

Using it with Build Advisor

Build Advisor and Loot Advisor are separate mods; each works on its own. Installed together, Loot Advisor uses the build you picked in Build Advisor for each character, so the items it recommends match the build you follow. Build Advisor is at https://github.com/md12ol/BuildAdvisor.

Both read the game and never change your character. Treat them as a guide with spoilers: they name builds, item locations and the story choices that open or close them.

Loot Advisor

Loot Advisor shows the rare items that best fit the character you have selected, and how to get them. Recommended items get a rainbow frame, their locations get rainbow diamonds on the map, and an item list (F6) explains each one. A Sets page in your browser shows full loadouts and follows your game live.

It covers the seven origin characters: Astarion, Gale, Karlach, Lae'zel, Shadowheart, Wyll and the Dark Urge. Advice follows that character's actual build, the current act, your story choices and what the party already owns. Items that need a theft, a kill or a story choice are included with a warning.

Requirements and install

NeedsScript Extender v33+
for frames and map painting; the list and Sets page work on v32
OptionalBuild Advisor
your build pick there is used to break ties
Disk3.75 MB pak
+ about 18 MB for the Sets page, built on first load
  1. Install Script Extender. Item frames and map painting need v33 or newer. Until v33 is a normal release, get it from the Devel channel: create a file ScriptExtenderUpdaterConfig.json in the game's bin folder containing {"UpdateChannel": "Devel"}, then start the game once. Delete that file to go back to normal releases.
  2. Import LootAdvisor.pak with BG3 Mod Manager and enable it (or copy it to the game's Mods folder and enable it in the game's mod manager).
  3. Start the game and load a save. Tick Loot Advisor if the Mod Verification dialog lists it. The console prints [Loot Advisor] loaded - F6 toggles the item list.
  4. Select an origin character. Frames and map markers appear within about a second; press F6 for the list.
  5. For the Sets page, open %LOCALAPPDATA%\Larian Studios\Baldur's Gate 3\Script Extender\LootAdvisor\Sets.html in your browser and bookmark it (F6 > Open Sets page shows this path, ready to copy). The console prints a line when the page is ready (about 8 seconds after the first load, under a second later on).

Uninstall. Turn markers off first ("Enabled": false in the settings, see Settings), then save, then disable the mod. Shown map markers are part of the game's journal state and may be stored in a save made while they were visible. Removing the mod from such a save has not been tested yet. Tooltip texts and frames are never saved. To clean up fully, delete the LootAdvisor folder and LootAdvisor_settings.json in the Script Extender folder.

Signs in the game

Rainbow frame on items

A recommended item gets a rainbow "prism" frame instead of the game's rarity frame. It shows wherever the item appears: inventory and bags, equipment slots on the character sheet, the hotbar, opened containers, the camp chest, the inventory search view and your side of the trade window. A bag that holds a recommended item gets the frame too. When the item stops being recommended, the game's own frame comes back.

Framed: items you own, items with a map marker, set items, items in another area and items with no fixed spot. Not framed: items whose story path is closed, items better kept for another companion, and items shown only in the list (random loot, generic +1 / +2 gear), which get no frame and no tooltip row either.

Rainbow diamond on the map

Each item to fetch gets a marker on the minimap and the world map (M). It looks like the game's gold quest diamond, in rainbow colours. Hover it for its label:

Map label
Sword of Chaos
Helldusk Gloves
Elixir of Viciousness

The label shows the rainbow diamond and a plain list of the items you can get there, one per line, in the same cyan as the tooltip advice. A character's name is added only when markers cover several characters (planned). Hovering the marker shows a Loot Advisor title with the rainbow diamond above that list.

Markers show the best and runner-up item per slot for the current act, for the character you have selected. Select someone else and the markers switch to that character. Once the party owns an item, its marker disappears; the frame stays.

Off-screen arrows

When a marked item is outside the minimap, the game draws its own off-screen arrow at the minimap rim, recoloured in rainbow. Only the 5 best markers get an arrow (best before runner-up, then in slot order), so the rim does not fill up. Items visible on the minimap show the diamond and no arrow. The world map does the same at its edges.

Entrance and region-exit markers

Many items lie inside places you cannot see from outside: vaults, cellars, the House of Hope, the Guildhall. For those, the marker goes on the entrance on the shortest way from where you stand: a door, ladder, hatch or portal. If the item is two areas deep, the marker sits on the first entrance on the way. Step inside and the marker moves to the next entrance, or to the item itself.

An item in another region (for example Wyrm's Crossing while you are in the Lower City) gets a marker on the way out of this region: a gate, lift or other region exit. Where no walking route leads there, the nearest waypoint is marked: fast travel from there. Several items behind the same entrance share one marker, and its label lists them all.

Advice in item tooltips

Hover a recommended item: under the game's description, one extra row appears, laid out like the tooltip's own rows. The rainbow diamond sits in the icon column at the size of the game's icons, and the text is cyan, a colour the game does not use in its descriptions. The row has at most two lines:

Tooltip row, examples
Best Gloves for Astarion
On your map · +1 attack rolls; grants Garrotte
Runner-up Armour for Karlach
Better on Lae'zel
Set Cloak for Gale
In another area · Community pick
LineWhat it says
1Best, Runner-up or Set, the slot, and the character it is for.
2-4The most important of: "Better on X"; "Path closed: …"; "Shared pick with X"; the item's warning (a theft, a kill, a story choice or a missable item) in a short form of up to three lines that keeps every name, act and cost; otherwise the status ("You have it", "On your map", "In another area", "No fixed spot (see F6)", "Only if you already have it") and a short reason.

The full reason, all warnings, the sets and how to get it are in the F6 list and on the Sets page. The row follows the selected character, is never stored in your save, and applies to every copy of the same item. Items shown only in the list get no row. It appears wherever the game shows an item tooltip: your bags, both sides of the trade window, pickpocketing, a corpse's loot and the camp chest. For the Dark Urge it uses your character's own name.

The item list (F6)

Press F6 to show or hide the list. It covers everything, including items that have no marker. Directions update every second while it is open.

Header

Line 1 (gold): character, act and the build Loot Advisor matched to the character. Line 2 (grey): the region, the number of items and markers, and the hotkey. Hover line 2 for why that build was picked (for example "closest to your class levels" or "closest to your classes; Build Advisor's order").

Open Sets page sits above the header. The game cannot open a browser or write to the clipboard, so the button shows the page's path in a field instead: click the field (it selects the whole path), press Ctrl+C, then paste it into your browser's address bar, or press Win+R, Ctrl+V, Enter. The same button hides the path again.

A character Loot Advisor does not cover shows one grey line instead:

Legend

A folded Legend section at the top of the list explains the marks and status words.

"Next – nearest items you can get now"

Up to six marked items, nearest first: item, slot, direction and distance from the selected character (compass point and metres, north = up on the minimap), and where the marker leads ("Enter Murder Tribunal", "Way out to Wyrm's Crossing", "On your map: Sorcerous Sundries"). Hover "where" for the full how-to text.

"All recommended items" – the columns

Story paths and the party

Story-path gating. Loot Advisor reads your game's story state: Shadowheart's Shar or Selûne path, whether the goblins raided the Grove or the tieflings were saved, Isobel's fate at Last Light, whether Mizora was freed, the Murder Tribunal, who is dead, and whether this is a Dark Urge campaign. An item behind a closed path is greyed with the reason, for example path closed: needs Shadowheart's Shar path or lost: Isobel's death (Last Light falls) happened. Dark Urge-only items read "Dark Urge campaign only" in other campaigns.

Items that cost a companion. An item whose price is losing one of the origin companions is left out completely, unless that has already happened in your game.

"Better on X". Some items are unique. Each unique item has one best owner, based on how much each build gets from it, decided among your active party (the up to four characters with you; companions waiting in camp don't count). Other characters see the item greyed as "Better on X", and their runner-up moves up. The item list, the tooltips, the map markers and the Sets page all decide it the same way.

Shared picks. When two characters fit a unique item exactly equally, neither is told to give it up. Both see "(shared)" in the Pick column and "Shared pick with …" in the tooltip: you decide who wears it.

Owned items count from the party's inventories and bags, members waiting in camp, and every camp chest. An item turns to "Owned" within about a second of picking it up.

The Sets page

A local web page that ships with the mod and shows complete loadouts ("synergy sets") for each origin character and act: about 240 sets in total. Open it in Chrome, Edge or Firefox while you play. It updates by itself; there is no folder to pick, no file to load and no extra program.

No game art ships with the mod. On your first load the mod builds the page's icons, fonts and item texts from your own game install, in your game's language. Loot Advisor's own advice text is in English.

Parts of the page

PartWhat it does
Act buttons I · II · IIISets are per act. Items of earlier acts appear only as "if you have it".
Live indicatorLive (green dot): connected, time of the last change, act, region, nearby area and selected character. Game not running (red dot): no update for 25 seconds; the page shows the last known state. Waiting for the game: nothing received yet.
My playthroughDark Urge playthrough, Grove fight, Shadowheart and the Nightsong, Isobel at Last Light, Theft and killing neutrals. Each reads "From your game: …"; choosing a value overrides it, and Use my game for everything drops the overrides. Hide earlier-act items I don't have removes items you can no longer get.
Character portraitsThe seven origin characters. The one selected in the game opens by itself, on the set of the build closest to the character's real classes.
Set listSets in order: main build, community builds, auto-picked sets. Chips: Main pick, Alternative 1–2, Option N; Community build or Auto-picked; "11/11 available" with your settings; coloured pills count story, crime, missable, earlier-act and party items.
Shopping listWhat to fetch: missable items first, then grouped along the act's route, earlier-act items last. Each row has a Have it tick, the slot, ◆ core for the item the set is built around, where to get it and coloured notes (Theft / kill, Missable, Tip, Party).
Equipment and sheetA paperdoll like the game's; hover an item for a game-style tooltip with Loot Advisor's notes on top. The character sheet (abilities, AC, HP, attacks, spell DC, resistances, granted actions) is computed at the character's real level; hover any number for its formula. Level 12 switches to the end-game numbers.
What the badges meanThe full legend: red triangle (story choice, theft, killing a neutral), orange triangle (missable or tip), ↻ earlier act, party conflict, ⇄ swapped by your settings, rarity colours, green raised scores.
Compare two setsPick A and B; differing slots get a dashed outline, and a delta column shows ▲ better / ▼ worse, plus counts of story locks, thefts and missables.

Live sync

While the game runs, the mod writes a small state file at most every 2 seconds when something changes (items picked up or moved, level-ups, party changes, story flags, deaths, a new save loaded, the selected character, a new area) and every 10 seconds anyway. The page re-reads it every 3 seconds and at once when you switch to its tab. A pickup in the game shows on the page within about 3–5 seconds.

  • Have it ticks fill from the party, camp members and camp chests ("In your game", with who holds it on hover). Manual ticks still work for other items.
  • Contested items follow your active party: if someone in the party gets more from an item, this character's slot uses the alternative; an exact tie is a Shared pick.
  • The character sheet uses the character's real level.

How items are picked

How the advice was made: scoring every item

Every weapon, armour piece and accessory in the game was read from the game files with its stats, effects and where it comes from. Each item is then scored for each build of each origin character, per act:

  • Usable at all? Armour and weapons the build is not proficient with are dropped, unless the item grants the proficiency. Build rules apply (no shield for a Monk, no heavy armour for a Bladesinger).
  • Build fit. Rarity; for weapons, how well the weapon matches the build's attack style plus its damage and enchantment; for armour, the AC the build really gets with its Dexterity (or its Unarmoured Defence); then every effect of the item, weighted by what the build needs. Effects with a condition the build doesn't arrange count less. Race-only effects count only for that race. Known Patch 8 bugs are scored as the game behaves, and the "why" text says so.
  • Community picks. Items named in popular build guides for that build get extra points (best pick, runner-up, part of a set), up to a cap.
  • Act. An item counts from the first act it can reliably be obtained in (world, container, reward, trader, NPC) to the last act it can still be obtained in.

That gives a best and runner-up per slot per act, and the synergy sets: sets taken from community builds, plus an auto-picked "best overall" loadout and theme sets that reach at least 85% of its score. Every set is legal: two-handed weapons keep the off hand empty, dual wielding needs light weapons, and no set mixes items whose story paths exclude each other. Items with a condition get a fallback; unique items get a party owner and an alternative for everyone else.

In the game: matching your character

Build matching. The selected character's live classes, subclasses and levels are compared with each of that character's builds. A class the build uses scores its levels (up to the build's own); a matching subclass adds a bonus; levels in classes the build doesn't use count against it. The highest score wins. On a tie, Build Advisor's pick for that character wins, then Build Advisor's build order. With no class in common, the build is chosen by the character's highest ability.

Recommending. For the matched build and the current act (taken from the region you are in), each slot's best and runner-up are checked against your game: owned, path closed, better on someone else, earlier act, random loot. If a pick is unusable, the next candidate moves up. Set slots follow the same rules, with these swaps:

  • in a Dark Urge campaign, a Dark Urge-only item that beats the set's pick replaces it;
  • an earlier-act item the party owns that is better replaces it;
  • otherwise the set's fallback is used.

Markers are shown for the best and runner-up of each slot that have a fixed spot in this region. Items in another area or region are routed to an entrance or exit (shortest way from the selected character, re-checked when you move into another area). Frames go on everything recommended that isn't random loot, closed, or better on someone else.

When it updates. The recommendation is recomputed when items move, a story flag is set, someone dies, the selection or a level changes, or you enter another area, and every 20 seconds otherwise. A recompute takes about 20–40 ms. Frames and marker colours are repainted twice a second (4–16 ms).

Settings

Settings live in LootAdvisor_settings.json in the Script Extender folder. The mod re-reads the file every few seconds, so edits apply without a restart. Only keys you want to change need to be in it.

KeyDefaultMeaning
EnabledtrueMaster switch. false hides all markers, restores frames and tooltip texts.
HotkeyF6Key for the item list.
FramestrueRainbow frames on items.
MarkerstrueMap markers.
Tooltipstrue"Why" text in item tooltips.
Arrows5How many off-screen markers keep a rainbow arrow.
UnsafeUiOnOldSEfalsetrue draws frames, tooltip lines and map painting on Script Extender older than v33 anyway. Older versions change the interface while the game draws it, which can crash the game (seen in combat); use v33 instead.
Pagetruefalse stops writing the Sets page and its live state.
ActOverridenoneForce act 1, 2 or 3 instead of the one detected from your region.
NorthZ, EastX1Set to -1 to flip the list's compass if directions ever look mirrored.

Known limitations

  • Origin characters only. Halsin, Jaheira, Minsc, Minthara, hirelings and custom characters show "not covered" and get no markers or frames.
  • One character at a time. Markers and frames follow the selected character. Markers for the whole party are planned.
  • Some items have no fixed spot (quest rewards, boss drops, forge results) and appear in the list only. A few traders are marked on the trader in person; the game draws those only when you are near them.
  • Areas are recognised from where things are placed in the level. Rarely, an interior is not recognised and the marker stays on the item itself, which then shows as an edge arrow.
  • "Fast travel" routes are checked offline only.
  • Map markers may be stored in a save made while they were shown; removing the mod from a save is not tested yet (see Uninstall).
  • Controller mode and the low-resolution interface are not tested.
  • Advice texts are English. Item names and game texts on the Sets page follow your game language.
  • The tooltip shows a shortened warning (up to three lines); the full text is in the F6 list and on the Sets page.
  • The list window uses * instead of the diamond, because its font has no diamond.
  • Item names in the in-game list are English; the Sets page uses your game language.
  • The Sets page: Chrome and Edge slow down tabs hidden for more than about 5 minutes (updates then arrive within a minute, and at once when you switch to the tab; Firefox keeps polling). Each page open needs 3–4 seconds to build its images. The area name is approximate ("near …"). In multiplayer only the host writes the page.

FAQ

I see no frames or markers.

Select one of the seven origin characters, and press F6: the header says which character and build Loot Advisor is using, or "not covered". Check that Enabled, Frames and Markers are not set to false.

Why is an item I want greyed out?

Hover its status. "Path closed" names the story choice, "Better on X" names the companion who gets more from it, "If you have it" means it is from an earlier act.

The marker is on a door, not on the item.

The item is inside that area. Go through the marked entrance; the marker moves on. "Way out marked" means the item is in another region.

Two characters both want the same unique item.

If one fits it better, the other sees "Better on X" and moves to the next pick. If they fit it equally, both see "shared pick" and you decide.

Does it spoil the story?

It names item locations, holders and the story choices that open or close them. Treat it as a guide with spoilers.

Can I trust the Sets page numbers?

They are computed from the game's own item and class rules; hover a number to see its formula. Some class features (Rage, Sneak Attack, smites, spells such as Shield) are not added.

The Sets page says "Game not running".

No update for 25 seconds: the game is closed, still loading, or Page is false. It catches up as soon as the game writes again.
